# Vocabulary register

Register `stoa-vocabulary`, version `0.1.0-m0`.

**Status:** provisional; L0 evidence-complete and ready to freeze (see spec/EVIDENCE.md)

30 elements at L0, 10 at L1, 8 at L2, 2 at L3. Total 50, plus 5 render primitives that are not document elements.

A document element above L0 declares the element it degrades into. That declaration is normative and mechanically tested: `stoa0.py <doc> contract` projects the whole document to L0 and asserts that no unit of reader-visible content is lost.

L0 is therefore not a reduced or lossy view. It is the layer every other layer is defined against, and the projection into it is normative output rather than best-effort extraction. Any consumer that wants meaning without presentation reads it directly: a screen reader, a terminal client, an archival indexer, or an autonomous agent. Those are one consumer with one guarantee, which is why non-visual targets are siblings in this design rather than accommodations.

## Field types

- `text` — NFC-normalised Unicode string, non-empty unless stated
- `int` — signed integer, no floating point anywhere in the format
- `decimal` — scaled decimal: an integer significand and an integer scale, never a float
- `bool` — true or false
- `lang` — BCP 47 language tag
- `urn` — a document identifier URN
- `iri` — an absolute IRI. Permitted ONLY on fields the client never fetches without a reader action
- `path` — a same-origin relative reference. MUST NOT express a scheme, an authority, or a leading '//'. This is the fetch boundary
- `idref` — the id of another node in the same document
- `hash` — a lowercase hex SHA-256 content hash

## L0 — content

Frozen on release. No amendment process can alter this layer; if L0 is wrong the answer is a new epoch, never a change to this one.

| Element | Class | Children | Degrades to | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | root | `flow` | — | `id`:urn, `lang`:lang, `title`:text |
| `section` | block | `flow` | — | `id`?:text, `lang`?:lang |
| `heading` | block | `inline` | — | `level`:int [1..6] |
| `paragraph` | block | `inline` | — | — |
| `list` | block | `item` | — | `ordered`:bool, `start`?:int |
| `item` | block | `flow` | — | `id`?:text |
| `term-list` | block | `term, definition` | — | — |
| `term` | block | `inline` | — | — |
| `definition` | block | `flow` | — | — |
| `quote` | block | `flow` | — | `source`?:text |
| `code-block` | block | `text` | — | `language`?:text |
| `note` | block | `flow` | — | `id`:text |
| `figure` | block | `media, caption, table, code-block` | — | `id`?:text |
| `caption` | block | `inline` | — | — |
| `media` | block | `none` | — | `src`:path, `alt`:text, `kind`:text ∈ {image, audio, video} |
| `table` | block | `row, table-section, caption` | — | `summary`?:text, `id`?:text |
| `row` | block | `cell, header-cell` | — | — |
| `cell` | block | `flow` | — | `colspan`?:int, `rowspan`?:int |
| `header-cell` | block | `flow` | — | `colspan`?:int, `rowspan`?:int, `scope`?:text ∈ {row, column} |
| `text` | inline | `none` | — | `v`:text |
| `emphasis` | inline | `inline` | — | — |
| `strong` | inline | `inline` | — | — |
| `code` | inline | `text` | — | — |
| `link` | inline | `inline` | — | `href`:iri |
| `reference` | inline | `inline` | — | `target`:idref |
| `note-ref` | inline | `none` | — | `target`:idref |
| `quantity` | inline | `none` | — | `significand`:int, `scale`:int, `unit`:text |
| `power` | inline | `none` | — | `base`:text, `exponent`:text |
| `date` | inline | `none` | — | `value`:text, `precision`:text ∈ {year, month, day, minute, second} |
| `line-break` | inline | `none` | — | — |

Notes:

- **`document`** — The root. Exactly one per document. title is metadata, not the first heading.
- **`section`** — Nesting depth carries the outline. There is no numbered heading hierarchy to get wrong.
- **`heading`** — level is advisory for themes; the outline of record is section nesting.
- **`item`** — id is optional and exists because real bibliographies are cited entry by entry. Found by the RFC corpus; see m0/FINDINGS.md defect 8.
- **`term-list`** — Term/definition pairs. The workhorse for administrative record metadata.
- **`code-block`** — language is a hint. A client that does not know it renders plain text, which is conforming.
- **`note`** — Footnote body. Placed in document order; the theme decides where it appears.
- **`figure`** — Does not admit a 'rendering' child. A rendering degrades into a figure, so permitting the nesting would let a conforming document project into a non-conforming one. Found by M0; see m0/FINDINGS.md defect 3.
- **`media`** — src is a path, never an IRI. A document therefore cannot name a host the client contacts. See m0/FINDINGS.md defect 1. alt is required and must be non-empty; that is a build error, not an audit finding.
- **`header-cell`** — Header association is structural, so an unassociated data cell is unrepresentable rather than an audit finding.
- **`text`** — The only node that carries characters. Every content unit is one of these.
- **`link`** — The one place an absolute IRI is permitted, because the client resolves it only on a reader action. Clients MUST NOT speculatively resolve, prefetch, or preconnect.
- **`reference`** — Intra-document cross-reference. Never leaves the document, so never a request.
- **`quantity`** — value = significand x 10^-scale, exactly. Currency is representable without error. Floats are not representable at all, which is the point.
- **`power`** — Exponentiation, rendered as base^exponent. Added at L0 after the second corpus falsified the bet that superscripts are not load-bearing: 75 of 75 superscripts in 16 RFCs were exponents, and dropping them turns 2^64 into 264 inside normative range specifications. Semantic rather than presentational on purpose -- a superscript is appearance, an exponent is meaning, and only the latter can be carried by a format that does not carry appearance. The degradation is not invented: it is the notation the RFC plain-text renderings already use. Fields are text, not int, because real exponents include symbolic values such as n-24. See m0/FINDINGS.md defect 8.
- **`date`** — ISO 8601, with declared precision so a client never invents accuracy the record does not have.
- **`line-break`** — For addresses and verse, where the break is content. Not for spacing; spacing is a theme concern.

## L1 — structure

| Element | Class | Children | Degrades to | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `article` | block | `flow` | `section` | `id`?:text |
| `abstract` | block | `flow` | `section` | — |
| `contents` | block | `item` | `list` | — |
| `bibliography` | block | `item` | `list` | — |
| `citation` | inline | `inline` | `reference` | `target`:idref |
| `admonition` | block | `flow` | `section` | `kind`:text ∈ {note, warning, caution, important} |
| `sidebar` | block | `flow` | `section` | — |
| `signature-block` | block | `term, definition` | `term-list` | — |
| `provenance` | block | `term, definition` | `term-list` | — |
| `table-section` | block | `row` | `row` | `kind`:text ∈ {head, body, foot} |

Notes:

- **`article`** — A self-contained part of a compound document.
- **`contents`** — Table of contents. Degrades to an ordinary list of intra-document references.
- **`admonition`** — Degrades to a section whose heading is the kind label, so the salience survives as words rather than as colour.
- **`signature-block`** — Who signed, in what role, when. Structural because it is the part of an administrative record most often reduced to an image.
- **`provenance`** — Issuer, identifier, timestamps, digest. Machine-readable custody without a second metadata format.
- **`table-section`** — Degrades by splicing its rows into the parent table in order.

## L2 — interaction

| Element | Class | Children | Degrades to | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `form` | block | `field, submit, heading, paragraph` | `section` | `action`:path, `method`:text ∈ {get, post} |
| `field` | block | `field-text, field-choice` | `term` | `name`:text, `label`:text, `required`?:bool |
| `field-text` | block | `none` | `paragraph` | `multiline`?:bool, `value`?:text |
| `field-choice` | block | `field-option` | `list` | `multiple`?:bool |
| `field-option` | block | `inline` | `item` | `value`:text, `selected`?:bool |
| `submit` | block | `none` | `paragraph` | `label`:text |
| `disclosure` | block | `flow` | `section` | `summary`:text, `open`?:bool |
| `state-link` | inline | `inline` | `link` | `key`:text, `value`:text |

Notes:

- **`form`** — action is a path, so a form cannot post across origins. Submission is always a reader action. Degrades to a section in which each run of degraded fields is wrapped in a term-list, so the projection is itself conforming L0.
- **`field`** — label is a required field, not a sibling element, so an unlabelled control cannot be expressed. Degrades to a term/definition pair.
- **`disclosure`** — Collapsing is a reader affordance. Degraded, the content is simply present, which is the safe direction.
- **`state-link`** — Changes addressable document state. Because state is addressable, it degrades to an ordinary link to the same document in that state.

## L3 — typed rendering

| Element | Class | Children | Degrades to | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `payload` | invisible | `none` | — | `id`:text, `type`:text, `data`:text |
| `rendering` | block | `caption` | `figure` | `renderer`:hash, `payload`:idref, `fallback`:text |

Notes:

- **`payload`** — Typed data for a renderer. Integers and scaled decimals only; a float in a payload is a validation error. Carries no visible content, so it contributes nothing to the degradation contract. PROVISIONAL: no corpus can produce a typed renderer payload, so this element is unevidenced. It ships so L3 can be implemented and tested, and does not become normative until two independent implementations exist. See docs/GOVERNANCE.md section 4.
- **`rendering`** — renderer is a content hash, never a location, so an unknown renderer is never a network lookup. Degrades to a figure carrying the fallback text. PROVISIONAL: no corpus can produce a typed renderer payload, so this element is unevidenced. It ships so L3 can be implemented and tested, and does not become normative until two independent implementations exist. See docs/GOVERNANCE.md section 4.

## Render primitives

Not document elements and not part of the 52. These are what an L3 renderer emits into a device-independent display list. Text emitted by a renderer stays text.

| Primitive | Fields |
|---|---|
| `frame` | `w`:int, `h`:int |
| `polyline` | `points`:int[], `role`:text |
| `area` | `points`:int[], `role`:text |
| `glyph-run` | `x`:int, `y`:int, `role`:text, `v`:text |
| `tick` | `axis`:text, `at`:int, `label`:text |
